concepts.name: Tokens and context window
concepts.summary: Recall that models read and produce tokens rather than words and that the context window caps the combined input and output size.

concepts.name: Chat message roles
concepts.summary: Explain how system, user and assistant messages structure a conversation request and shape the model's behaviour.

concepts.name: Calling a completion API
concepts.summary: Understand the parts of an API request and response, including model name, messages, API key authentication and the returned text and usage.

concepts.name: Sampling parameters
concepts.summary: Explain how temperature, top-p and max output tokens change the randomness and length of generated output.

concepts.name: Basic prompt clarity
concepts.summary: Understand that specific instructions, context and a stated output format produce more reliable responses than vague requests.

concepts.name: Hallucination and model limits
concepts.summary: Recognise that models can produce confident but false output and lack knowledge of recent or private data.

concepts.name: Cost and latency drivers
concepts.summary: Recall that cost and response time grow with the number of input and output tokens and with model size.

misconceptions.text: The model looks up facts in a database, so its answers are always accurate.
Tokens are the same as words, so word count gives exact cost and limits.
The model remembers earlier API calls on its own without being sent the conversation again.

concepts.name: Few-shot prompting
concepts.summary: Apply worked input-output examples in a prompt to steer format, tone and task behaviour.

concepts.name: Prompt templates with variables
concepts.summary: Build reusable prompts that insert user data into fixed instructions in code.

concepts.name: JSON output parsing
concepts.summary: Request JSON output, parse it in Python and validate it against a schema such as a Pydantic model.

concepts.name: Streaming responses
concepts.summary: Consume partial output as it is generated to improve perceived latency in an application.

concepts.name: API error and rate-limit handling
concepts.summary: Handle timeouts, rate limits and server errors with retries, exponential backoff and clear failures.

concepts.name: Multi-turn conversation state
concepts.summary: Maintain and trim the message history sent on each call so conversations stay coherent within the context window.

concepts.name: Secret and key management
concepts.summary: Keep API keys out of source code and client-side code by using environment variables or a secrets store.

misconceptions.text: Asking for JSON in the prompt guarantees the output is always valid and matches the schema.
Retrying immediately and repeatedly is the right way to handle rate limit errors.
Few-shot examples teach the model permanently, so they only need to be sent once.

concepts.name: Embeddings and semantic similarity
concepts.summary: Use embedding vectors and a similarity measure to find text with related meaning.

concepts.name: Document chunking strategies
concepts.summary: Analyse how chunk size, overlap and boundaries affect retrieval quality and choose a splitting approach for a corpus.

concepts.name: Vector store indexing and search
concepts.summary: Store embeddings with metadata and query for top-k neighbours with filters.

concepts.name: Retrieval-augmented generation pipeline
concepts.summary: Assemble ingestion, indexing, retrieval and grounded generation, and trace failures to the right stage.

concepts.name: Tool calling and function schemas
concepts.summary: Define tool schemas, execute the calls the model requests and return results for the final answer.

concepts.name: Grounding and citation prompts
concepts.summary: Design prompts that restrict answers to retrieved context, cite sources and admit when information is missing.

concepts.name: Evaluation datasets and metrics
concepts.summary: Build a labelled test set and choose metrics such as exact match, retrieval recall and rubric scores to compare prompt changes.

concepts.name: Prompt injection risks
concepts.summary: Analyse how untrusted user or retrieved text can override instructions and apply basic mitigations.

misconceptions.text: Larger chunks always improve RAG because they give the model more context.
The model executes the functions itself when it makes a tool call.
Telling the model to use only the provided context completely eliminates hallucination.

concepts.name: Hybrid search and reranking
concepts.summary: Combine keyword and vector retrieval and rerank candidates, judging the precision and latency trade-offs.

concepts.name: Query rewriting and decomposition
concepts.summary: Transform conversational or complex questions into effective retrieval queries.

concepts.name: Component-level RAG evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate retrieval (recall, MRR) and generation (faithfulness, relevance) separately to locate defects.

concepts.name: LLM-as-judge evaluation
concepts.summary: Judge when model-based graders are valid by calibrating them against human labels and controlling for bias.

concepts.name: Agent loops and orchestration
concepts.summary: Design loops where the model plans and calls tools across steps, with step limits, state and error recovery.

concepts.name: Caching and cost optimisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate caching, model selection and prompt trimming to reduce cost and latency with acceptable quality.

concepts.name: Observability and tracing
concepts.summary: Instrument calls to capture prompts, outputs, tool steps, latency and cost so failures can be diagnosed.

concepts.name: Guardrails and output validation
concepts.summary: Assess and apply input and output checks, schema validation and fallbacks for safety and reliability.

misconceptions.text: Vector search alone is always enough, so keyword search adds nothing.
An LLM judge's scores are objective and need no validation against human judgement.
A good end-to-end answer score shows both retrieval and generation are working.

concepts.name: Architecture trade-off design
aliases: RAG vs fine-tuning vs long context
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether prompting, retrieval, fine-tuning or long context best fits a requirement given cost, freshness and accuracy.

concepts.name: Fine-tuning and distillation decisions
concepts.summary: Judge when adapting or distilling a model beats prompting and plan the data and evaluation needed.

concepts.name: Continuous evaluation pipelines
concepts.summary: Create evaluation systems combining offline regression suites, production sampling and user feedback that gate releases.

concepts.name: Multi-agent system design
concepts.summary: Design systems of cooperating agents with defined roles, shared state, permissions and failure containment.

concepts.name: Security threat modelling for LLMs
concepts.summary: Evaluate risks such as indirect prompt injection, excessive tool permissions and data leakage and design layered defences.

concepts.name: Reliability under model change
concepts.summary: Assess the effect of model updates and provider outages and design pinning, fallbacks and migration tests.

concepts.name: Feedback-driven improvement loops
concepts.summary: Create processes that turn production failures and user signals into new test cases, prompt changes and training data.

misconceptions.text: Fine-tuning is the best way to add new knowledge to a model's answers.
More agents with more autonomy always yield better results on complex tasks.
Once prompts pass the evaluation suite, behaviour stays stable across model updates.
